name: WS2812B light bar, 5 pixels at 60 LEDs/m (83 mm cut)
blurb: Five addressable RGB pixels cut from one strip, in a row, driven by a single data line. Shows the device state through the lid.

pins.name: 5V
pins.note: Needs 5 V. Five pixels draw up to about 300 mA at full white; this build caps brightness in firmware (see peakMa on the part).

pins.name: DIN
pins.note: Data in, the pad marked DIN at the input end. Needs 3.5 V to read a high on a 5 V strip; the 3.3 V controller pin is outside the datasheet and is accepted here for a short run (see the hand-over).

pins.name: GND
pins.note: Connect GND before 5 V when hot-plugging.

verify: Built as a 5-pixel cut of the library strip ws2812b-strip (same pad layout at the input end). Buy a strip at 60 LEDs/m, cut 5 pixels (about 83 mm, pixel pitch 16.7 mm), and check the pad order printed on the strip (5V DIN GND is typical; some print GND DIN 5V). Measure the strip width (10 mm) and the pixel pitch before printing the lid: the light-bar window is 80 mm long and must sit over the pixels.
sources: Pad layout, supply range and current: assets/parts/ws2812b-strip.json (WS2812B datasheet via Adafruit mirror, opened in the library file)
Pixel pitch 16.7 mm: 60 LEDs/m, common strip. Light-bar length is this project's own choice.
